rubric_items.reason: All nine ticket acceptance criteria map to REQ-1..REQ-12, including the hospital time zone; API filter design is out of scope with a reason.
Most REQs are atomic and checkable; REQ-7 bundles search, status filter and sort order into one requirement.
Every REQ cites a ticket line; the meaning of registered is decided by the user's answer A-01 and cited; no invented values.
No clash between ticket and baseline; the undefined term registered was raised as Q-01 and answered.
Q-01 was precise with real options, but the tension between keeping the status filter and listing Inactive patients was noted as a risk without a question.
Plain words; glossary terms Period, Tile, Inactive used consistently; missing glossary term registered is noted.

findings.text: REQ-7 is a compound requirement: it covers three separate behaviours (search kept, status filter kept, sort order kept) that a tester checks independently.

cites.quote: Filtered list keeps search, status and sort

findings.suggested_fix: Split REQ-7 into three REQs: filtered list keeps current search; keeps current status filter; keeps current sort order.

findings.text: The artifact names a risk that keeping the list's current status filter may hide the Inactive patients the tile counts (REQ-3, REQ-5), but raises no question on which wins; ask missing.
